cards.front:
**Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.since() / Overview**

Explain the key points of Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.since(), including any stated conditions or limitations.
cards.back:
<!-- recall:teaching:v1 -->

## Explanation

The **`since()`** method of `Temporal.PlainDateTime` instances returns a new `Temporal.Duration` object representing the duration from another date-time (in a form convertible by `Temporal.PlainDateTime.from()`) to this date-time. The duration is positive if the other date-time is before this date-time, and negative if after.

This method does `this - other`. To do `other - this`, use the `until()` method.

---
Adapted from [MDN contributors](https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/3a04b53622d472799bacec2b79ef7bd44b43f1d9/files/en-us/web/javascript/reference/global_objects/temporal/plaindatetime/since/index.md). [CC BY-SA 2.5; code CC0 or MIT](/licenses/library-mdn--content.txt). Prompts, formatting, and selected wording adapted for Recall; source license applies to this material.

cards.front:
**Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.since() / Syntax / Parameters**

Explain Syntax / Parameters in the context of Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.since().
cards.back:
<!-- recall:teaching:v1 -->

## Explanation

- `other`
  - : A string, an object, or a `Temporal.PlainDateTime` instance representing a date-time to subtract from this date-time. It is converted to a `Temporal.PlainDateTime` object using the same algorithm as `Temporal.PlainDateTime.from()`. It must have the same calendar as `this`.
- `options` (optional)
  - : An object containing the options for `Temporal.Duration.prototype.round()`, which includes `largestUnit`, `roundingIncrement`, `roundingMode`, and `smallestUnit`. `largestUnit` and `smallestUnit` accept all possible units. For `largestUnit`, the default value `"auto"` means `"days"` or `smallestUnit`, whichever is greater. For `smallestUnit`, the default value is `"nanoseconds"`. The current date is used as the `relativeTo` option. Note that using [units larger than `"days"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Temporal/Duration#calendar_durations) may make the duration not portable to other calendars or dates.

---
Adapted from [MDN contributors](https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/3a04b53622d472799bacec2b79ef7bd44b43f1d9/files/en-us/web/javascript/reference/global_objects/temporal/plaindatetime/since/index.md). **Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.subtract() / Overview**

Explain the key points of Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.subtract(), including any stated conditions or limitations.
cards.back:
<!-- recall:teaching:v1 -->

## Explanation

The **`subtract()`** method of `Temporal.PlainDateTime` instances returns a new `Temporal.PlainDateTime` object representing this date-time moved backward by a given duration (in a form convertible by `Temporal.Duration.from()`).

If you want to subtract two date-times and get a duration, use `since()` or `until()` instead.

---
Adapted from [MDN contributors](https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/3a04b53622d472799bacec2b79ef7bd44b43f1d9/files/en-us/web/javascript/reference/global_objects/temporal/plaindatetime/subtract/index.md). cards.front:
**Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.subtract() / Syntax / Parameters**

Explain Syntax / Parameters in the context of Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.subtract().
cards.back:
<!-- recall:teaching:v1 -->

## Explanation

- `duration`
  - : A string, an object, or a `Temporal.Duration` instance representing a duration to subtract from this date-time. It is converted to a `Temporal.Duration` object using the same algorithm as `Temporal.Duration.from()`.
- `options` (optional)
  - : An object containing the following property:
    - `overflow` (optional)
      - : A string specifying the behavior when a date component is out of range. Possible values are:
        - `"constrain"` (default)
          - : The date component is [clamped](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Temporal/PlainDate#invalid_date_clamping) to the valid range.
        - `"reject"`
          - : A `RangeError` is thrown if the date component is out of range.

---

## Explanation

The `toJSON()` method is automatically called by `JSON.stringify()` when a `Temporal.PlainDateTime` object is stringified. cards.front:
**Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.toLocaleString() / Syntax / Return value**

What does Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.toLocaleString() return?
cards.back:
<!-- recall:teaching:v1 -->

## Explanation

A string representing the given date-time according to language-specific conventions.

In implementations with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, this is equivalent to `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locales, options).format(dateTime)`, where `options` has been normalized as described above.

> Most of the time, the formatting returned by `toLocaleString()` is consistent. However, the output may vary between implementations, even within the same locale — output variations are by design and allowed by the specification. It may also not be what you expect. For example, the string may use non-breaking spaces or be surrounded by bidirectional control characters. You should not compare the results of `toLocaleString()` to hardcoded constants.

---
Adapted from [MDN contributors](https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/3a04b53622d472799bacec2b79ef7bd44b43f1d9/files/en-us/web/javascript/reference/global_objects/temporal/plaindatetime/tolocalestring/index.md). **Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.toZonedDateTime() / Syntax / Exceptions**

Under what conditions does Temporal.PlainDateTime.prototype.toZonedDateTime() throw an exception?
cards.back:
<!-- recall:teaching:v1 -->

## Explanation

- `RangeError`
  - : Thrown in one of the following cases:
    - Any of the options is invalid.
    - `timeZone` is not a valid time zone identifier.
    - The wall-clock time is ambiguous in the time zone, and `options.disambiguation` is set to `"reject"`.
- `TypeError`
  - : Thrown if any of the arguments are not of the expected type.
